label: a
alt_text: Stacked time series of total widow rockfish catches, showing low catches up to 1979, a peak around 1980 averaging around 30000 tons, an average around 10000 tons from 1983 to the late 1990s, low catches from there up to 2016, and average around 10000 tons again from 2017 to 2024. See Table 10 for values.

label: b
alt_text: Starting in 1916, spawning output was about 21.1 trillion eggs, fell to a low of about 4.6 trillion in 1998, rose to a 2010s high of about 15.4 trillion in 2017, and was about 10.6 trillion in 2025. See Table 20 for values.

label: c
alt_text: The fraction of unfished spawning output dropped to a low of about 0.22 in 1998, rose to a high of 0.73 in 2017 and ended around 0.5 in 2025. See Table 20 for values.

label: d
alt_text: The range of age-0 recruitment estimates was from a low of about 9 million in 2012 to about 132 million in 1970 with 2025 at about 37 million which is close to the long-term median. See Table 20 for values.

label: e
alt_text: Phase plot shows counter-clockwise spiral with final point in the upper-right quadrant indicating that the stock is currently above the SPR target but above the target fraction unfished. Uncertainty is strongly negatively correlated such that lower fraction unfished is associated with higher relative fishing intensity. See Table 20 for values.

label: catches-all
alt_text: Stacked time series of total widow rockfish catches, showing low catches up to 1979, a peak around 1980 averaging around 30000 tons, an average around 10000 tons from 1983 to the late 1990s, low catches from there up to 2016, and average around 10000 tons again from 2017 to 2024. See Table 10 for values.

label: data-plot-base
alt_text: Timeline-style plot showing which data sources by type and year were used in the base model with catches extending back to 1916 but most other data sources starting in the 1970s or later.

label: qq-sdmtmb
alt_text: Two Q-Q plots compare model residual quantiles to theoretical quantiles for delta-gamma and delta-lognormal sdmTMB index fits. The presence/absence component is close to the one-to-one line, indicating a better fit, while the catch-rate component shows more deviation from the one-to-one line.

label: absurv-compare
alt_text: Colored lines showing similar trends among alternative statistical approaches to error standardization.

label: exp-lencomp-WCBTS
alt_text: Bubble plot showing noisy distribution with large amounts of variability in observed lengths among years.

label: cond-agelen-WCBTS
alt_text: Bubble plot showing similar patterns of age at length, with smaller length bins showing rapid growth up to around age 20 and larger bins showing a wide range of older ages up to 40.

label: lencomp-fleet1
alt_text: Bubble plot showing relatively consistent length compositions for the bottom trawl fishery with some evidence of large cohorts moving through the population and a mode around 40 cm.

label: lencomp-fleet2
alt_text: Similar bubble plot to the bottom trawl fishery above.

label: lencomp-fleet3
alt_text: Similar bubble plot to the bottom trawl and midwater fishery above, with slightly sparser samples.

label: agecomp-fleet1
alt_text: Bubble plot showing an average observed age around 10 years old with some diagonal patterns associated with large cohorts in the 1980s and more old fish in the most recent 10 years.

label: agecomp-fleet2
alt_text: Similar bubble plot to the bottom trawl fishery above except with fewer old fish in the years 2022 to 2024.

label: agecomp-fleet3
alt_text: Similar bubble plot to the midwater fishery above.

label: disc-hnl-comparison
alt_text: Bubble plot showing very different distributions of lengths and years covered between the two data sets.

label: wl-fits
alt_text: Two-panel comparison of female and male weight-at-length fits from prior and current assessments, with points showing observations and dashed lines showing fitted relationships. The fitted relationships are almost identical between assessments.

label: n-at-age
alt_text: Counts at age for female and male widow rockfish compiled across all age data sources, showing a mode for both sexes at age 6.

label: disc-hnl-update-ssb
alt_text: Time series declines to low point around 2000 for data updates, but final years differ with the HKL discards added for 2018 to 2023 showing a very high estimate of the spawning output in the last 5 years.

label: disc-hnl-update-depl
alt_text: Similar time series to previous plot in the scale of fraction unfished.

label: disc-hnl-update-rec
alt_text: Bridging time series of recruitment showing strong influence of treatment of hook-and-line discard treatment on recruitment in some recent years.

label: bridge2019-data
alt_text: Spawning biomass trajectories show that updating other data sources had relatively small impacts on the time series compared to the treatment of hook-and-line discards.

label: bridge2019-bratio
alt_text: Similar patterns to the previous plot but in the scale of fraction unfished, showing that the hook-and-line discard treatment had a large influence on the estimated fraction unfished trajectory.

label: bridge2-smrybio
alt_text: Age 4-plus biomass trajectories comparing bridging runs from the August 2025 model to the base model show similar patterns among models.

label: bridge2-bratio
alt_text: Relative spawning biomass trajectories show similar patterns among models with base model ending slightly below the fraction unfished of the August 2025 model.

label: bridge2-rec
alt_text: Recruitment trajectories show slightly higher recruitment in the models with updating data weighting, including the base model.

label: fecundity
alt_text: Fecundity-at-length curves show stronger dependence of spawning output on larger fish under fecundity-based relationships.

label: base_19_25_bratio
alt_text: Comparison of fraction unfished trajectories and 95 percent intervals between 2019 and 2025 base models show similar trends and uncertainty until around 2017 when the base model starts a steady decline but the 2019 model extended upwards.

label: base_19_25_smry
alt_text: Comparison of age-4-plus trajectories show the scale of the 2025 base model is slightly below that of the 2019 assessment and also declines from about 2017 onward instead of continuing to increase.

label: base_19_25_recr
alt_text: Recruitment comparisons show that the 2019 assessment had a much higher estimate of recruitment in 2013 while the 2016 recruitment is higher in the 2025 base model (though still about half as high as the 2019 estimate of 2016 recruitment).

label: base_19_25_recdevs
alt_text: Comparison of log recruitment deviation estimates with 95 percent intervals show that the intervals for the 2016 recruitment are not overlapping indicating how significant the change in estimates have been.

label: NatMort
alt_text: Figure shows biggest changes in estimates of M associated with updating the age composition (which led to lower M) and updating the weighting, which increased it somewhat, though base model estimates are still below 2019 and 2015 estimates. In all cases, the M estimates for males is higher than females, and both values are higher than the prior.

label: est-select-all
alt_text: Estimated selectivity curves showing increasing probability of capture by length with the hake fleet peaks at the smallest size among the fleets, while the WCGBTS peaks latest. The midwater trawl estimate is strongly dome-shaped while the others are completely or mostly asymptotic.

label: est-select-3478
alt_text: Time-block-specific selectivity curves for bottom trawl, midwater trawl, and hake fleets show the largest changes for the midwater fleet which was estimated as more asymptotic in the period of low catches from 2002 to 2016 but strongly dome-shaped before and after that interval.

label: sizeatage-sdcv
alt_text: Length-at-age relationship with estimated variability, showing that the CV of length at age is larger for smaller fish but the standard deviation is relatively constant across ages after about age 5.

label: recdev-est
alt_text: Time series of recruitment deviations in the upper panel show very uncertain estimates close to 0 from around 1900 to about 1970 with well-informed deviations up to about 2020 and imprecise values in the most recent years. The lower panel shows the same pattern on the non-log scale. See Table 20 for recruitment estimates.

label: recfit-bias
alt_text: Recruitment bias-adjustment ramp comparison shows the recruitment bias adjustment is higher for the informed period from about 1970 to 2020.

label: surv-abundest
alt_text: Fits to all indices are reasonable, with the Juvenile Survey showing the largest variability among years which is not captured by the relatively smooth line showing the model fit. The 1980s show declines in observed and expected values for some indices, while the WCGBTS shows an increase in observed and expected values from 2003 to 2016 and then a decline in both observed and expected values from 2017 to 2024 (with the observed values showing much more variability than the expected values in the most recent years).

label: lenage-pears-res-trawl
alt_text: Pearson residual bubble plots show few strong patterns although there are occasional blobs of larger residuals for males or females spanning a few ages and a few years.

label: comp-lenfit-aggreg
alt_text: Aggregated length frequency data show generally good fits for all fleets with the exceptions of the Triennial lengths, which show a lot of noise, and the unsexed samples from the bottom trawl fleet where the observed values have a narrower distribution.

label: comp-lenfit-trien
alt_text: Pearson residuals are small for both bottom trawl surveys.

label: combine-agefreq-all
alt_text: Aggregated age frequencies show good fits to age comps for all fleets. The observed modes are slightly more peaked than the estimated for males in all fleets, but the modes for females are very well matched.

label: condAAL-andreplot
alt_text: Complex plot from Andre Punt which is very difficult to interpret or describe but can be very helpful to confirm that the fit to the conditional age-at-length data is reasonable.

label: condAAL-resids
alt_text: Residuals for conditional age-at-length fits show relatively few large residuals. In the most recent years, the observed ages are older than expected for both females and males.

label: spawnout-95
alt_text: Similar time series to previous time series plots. See Table 20 for values.

label: summary-bio
alt_text: Similar time series to previous time series plots. See Table 20 for values.

label: rel-spawn-bio
alt_text: Similar time series to previous time series plots. See Table 20 for values.

label: SR-curve
alt_text: Stock-recruit curve is mostly flat over the range of estimated spawning output.

label: pred-one-SPR
alt_text: Time series of summary fishing mortality shows similar pattern to catch time series in previous plots, but F around 1980s is not as different as the catch because the abundance was higher at that time. F values in the recent years are slightly lower than the 1980s and 1990s in spite of similar catches because the abundance is estimated to be higher in recent years.

label: relative-one-SPR
alt_text: Phase plot shows counter-clockwise spiral with final point in the upper-right quadrant indicating that the stock is currently above the SPR target but above the target fraction unfished. Uncertainty is strongly negatively correlated such that lower fraction unfished is associated with higher relative fishing intensity.

label: spawnbio-sens-uncrt
alt_text: Sensitivity comparison of spawning output shows the biggest changes when natural mortality is fixed at higher or lower values than the base model.

label: depl-sens
alt_text: Patterns of fraction of unfished show similar patterns to previous plot, with only the M = 0.1 case falling below the 0.25 and 0.4 reference points in 2025.

label: rec-sens
alt_text: Spiky line plot showing that the scale of recruitment is strongly linked to natural mortality.

label: recdevs-sens
alt_text: Recruitment deviations show similar patterns except for the M = 0.1 case where  recruitment is below average from 1920 to 1965 suggesting that the model is using the uninformed period of recruitment to create out-of-equilibrium conditions in order to have the main time series better fit the data that are not consistent with this low M value.

label: retros
alt_text: Ten-year retrospective analysis shows very similar lines for each year of data removal with the recent recruitments closer to the long-term mean as the data are removed.

label: retros-squid
alt_text: Retrospective cohort lines of recruitment deviations show that below average recruitments are relatively well estimated by about age 5, but estimates of above average cohorts continue to evolve even after being observed up through age 10.

label: ssb-historical
alt_text: Similar lines for each assessment with different end points shows that the current assessments indicate the stock was below the 0.25 reference point in the 1990s compared to many other recent assessments which show the low point between 0.3 and 0.4.

label: like_profile_Rzero
alt_text: U-shaped profile curves showing R0 estimate is a balance of recruitment likelihood which is better fit at high R0 and the composition likelihoods which are better fit at lower R0. Index likelihoods are best fit at values close to the base model estimate. Patterns among fleets are inconsistent.

label: like_profile_Steepness
alt_text: Steepness profile shows best fit at high steepness values for all data types except length compositions. Patterns among fleets are consistent with better fit to age comps at high h for all fleets except bottom trawl and better fit to length comps at low h for all fleets.

label: like_profile_MF
alt_text: U-shaped profile curves indicate that recruitment and age data are the most significant contributors to the total likelihood with the age data supporting a lower M. Among fleets, the WCGBTS is best fit at the lowest M values (below 0.1) while the bottom trawl fleet is best fit around M = 0.16.

label: like_profile_MM
alt_text: Very similar patterns to the profiles over female M in the previous plot.

label: like_profile_recruits
alt_text: Recruitment deviations show that early, poorly-informed, recruitment deviations are influenced the most by alternative values for M.

label: est-eqi-yield
alt_text: Equilibrium yield curve and associated reference points show equilibrium yield is somewhat lower at the biomass target and the SPR targets than at MSY, but in all cases, the estimated yield is between 5000 and 7000 metric tons.

label: dec-table-plot
alt_text: Time series lines with uncertainty intervals show the low state ending below 0.25, the base model around 0.5, and the high state ending around 0.6.

label: vulnerable-bio
alt_text: Estimated vulnerable biomass by fleet shows that the differences in selectivity lead to much higher or lower estimates of the vulnerable biomass, with different trends associated with selecting different subsets of the population.

label: age-structure-2027
alt_text: Barplot shows the 2027 estimates have a big spike at age 11, but values well below the equilibrium for ages 7 to 9.
